sentences.text: Bench: Sunita Yadav  NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22003  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT GWALIOR  BEFORE  HON'BLE SMT. JUSTICE SUNITA YADAV  ON THE 11 th OF DECEMBER, 2024  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 22675 of 2024  ANURAG JATAV  Versus
THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Shri Ravindra Singh Rajpoot - advocate for the petition  Shri Yogesh Parashar- P.P. - appearing on behalf of Adv  Shri Mayaram Lodhi, learned counsel for the respondent   ORDER By invoking inherent power of this Court, present petition has been preferred by petitioners u/S.482 of Cr.P.C. seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 375/2023 registered at Police Station Mehgaon, District Bhind (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 363 added section 366, 366-A, 376 (2) (n) of IPC and section 5/6 of POCSO Act on the basis of compromise.

2. Alongwith the petition, both the parties have filed I.A No. 19330/2024 and I.A. No. 19331/2024,
stating therein that the dispute between the parties has been resolved and they have entered into compromise with no intention to pursue the matter further.

3. In compliance of order dated 12.09.2024 passed by this Court, the factum of compromise has been verified by the Principal Registrar of this Court, who has recorded the statements of complainant/respondent No.2 as well as the petitioner - accused and has submitted the report that the parties have arrived at compromise voluntarily without any threat, inducement and coercion.

sentences.text: 1 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that now the petitioner and prosecutrix have solemnized marriage and both are living as husband and wife and from their wedlock they are blessed with a child.

5. In the cases of Jagdish Channa & others Vs. State of Haryana & another (AIR 2008 SC 1968),
Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab (AIR 2008 SC 1969), Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another (2011)
10 SCC 705, and Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, Supreme Court has laid down that even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the Court can be saved and utilised in other material cases.
6.

sentences.text: In view of the above facts and circumstances and taking into account the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court, in the opinion of this court, continuance of the prosecution in such matters will be a futile exercise which will serve no purpose.
Under such a situation, Section 482 of Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the courts below.

7. Considering the fact that the respondent No.2 and petitioner - accused have amicably resolved the issue, this Court allows this MCRC with the following direction:-
8.

FIR dated 21.12.2023 bearing Crime No. 375/2023 registered at Police Station Mehgaon, District Bhind (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 363 added section 366, 366-A, 376 (2) (n) of IPC and section 5/6 of POCSO Act against the petitioner is hereby quashed only with respect to present petitioner.
9. All the consequential proceedings flowing out of the said FIR also stand quashed.

10. It is made clear that the instant FIR is being quashed only keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the present case and this order cannot be taken NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:22003 3 MCRC-22675-2024 as a precedent on the power of High Court to exercise its jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash an FIR on the ground that the complainant and the accused person have entered into a compromise.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE Durgekar Anurag Jatav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185889052/
